feature_candidates.description: Embedding or one-hot for tab id used as a per-item context bias in BPR scoring.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Moderate; tab strongly correlates with long_view but may encode exposure policy shifts.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Add tab as context feature to item or user-item interaction in BPR model.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Low; tab is in train/valid log but could be unstable across splits.

feature_candidates.description: Concatenate video duration and upload_type as side features in the BPR interaction embedding.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: Low-to-moderate; static features alone were flat but may complement embedding capacity.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Join video feature table on item id and feed into BPR embedding or MLP head.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Low; video features are static and fully observed.
feature_candidates.name: video_duration_upload_type

feature_candidates.description: Per-user long_view and click counts on the same video from train window, computed via history_features family.
feature_candidates.expected_impact: High; within-user same-item preference is strong, though possibly sparse for cold items.
feature_candidates.implementation_scope: Reuse history_features family to build per-user-item aggregates strictly on train data.
feature_candidates.leakage_risk: Low if train-only; must not include valid labels.
feature_candidates.name: same_video_past_qv

findings.title: Video duration and upload_type vary by engagement

findings.evidence: Leakage flag section in data card.
findings.implication: Use train-only counts as features instead of the leaky period-aggregate table.

findings.title: Train-only popularity proxies are legal and likely predictive

expected_artifacts: Univariate and bivariate distributions of long_view by tab, hourmin, video duration, upload_type (train only).
Correlation heatmap of candidate features with long_view residual after click model.
Train-only video popularity features (exposure count, long_view rate) with quantile plots.
Brief EDA report with recommended feature set to test in bpr/history_features families.
feature_hypotheses: Video duration and upload_type interact with user active degree to predict long_view; adding these as side features to BPR improves GAUC.
User's historical long_view rate on the same video (from history_features) is a strong within-user signal.
Time-of-day effects (hourmin buckets) are consistently discriminative across tabs and can be added as a per-video-tab bias.
Video popularity proxy from train-only exposure counts (not full-platform) can separate high- vs low-engagement items without leakage.
leakage_risks: Full-platform video statistics table is period-aggregate with 4892x ratio; any derived feature leaks future information.
Using test or future-period aggregates would violate split integrity.
User-level aggregates computed on the full train+valid could leak validation labels; only train-derived features are safe.
Positional features like tab or hour may encode exposure policy confounds that are not stable across splits.
plan.objective: Plan a leakage-safe EDA pass on train/valid to identify discriminative video- and interaction-based features for within-user long_view ranking, focusing on history, temporal, and context signals compatible with BPR/history_features families.
questions: What is the marginal impact of video duration, tab, and hour-of-day on long_view within-user after controlling for click?
How predictive are user's past long_view/click rates on the same video or same video category?
Does within-user exposure recency (days since last exposure to a video) correlate with subsequent long_view?
What is the distribution of long_view by hourmin and does it reveal strong diurnal patterns usable as biases?
required_inputs: Train/valid interaction logs with all static video/user features.
History_features family output: per-user-per-video past long_view/click counts.
Feature table with video duration, upload_type, and user profile fields (active_degree, is_live_streamer).
hourmin and tab fields from the log.

report.recommended_next_focus: Test BPR with tab bias and video duration/upload_type side features, then add history_features same-video past long_view; use seed 2 baseline (primary 0.6040) as reference.
report.summary: EDA plan analyzed train-only tab, hourmin, duration, upload_type, and popularity signals; recommends testing BPR side features (tab bias, duration/upload_type) and history_features for same-video past long_view, all leakage-safe.
ui_notes: Show univariate long_view rate per tab and hourmin bucket with row counts.
Plot train-only exposure count quantiles vs long_view rate for top-1000 videos.
